questions.q: How does Jaccard similarity score how alike two nodes are?
options: The size of the intersection of their connections divided by the size of the union of their connections
By counting each node's total number of properties
By measuring the physical distance between two nodes on disk
By running PageRank on both nodes and comparing the scores
questions.explain: Jaccard similarity is intersection over union — identical connection sets score 1.0, no overlap scores 0.0.

questions.q: When is cosine similarity preferred over Jaccard similarity for node similarity in GDS?
options: When the relationships carry a meaningful numeric weight, such as a star rating, that binary overlap alone wouldn't capture
Cosine similarity is always strictly better and should always be used instead of Jaccard
Cosine similarity only works on graphs with fewer than 10 nodes
There is no real difference between Jaccard and cosine similarity
questions.explain: Cosine similarity accounts for weighted connections (like ratings), capturing 'rates similarly' rather than just 'touched the same items.'

questions.q: In the plain Cypher 'customers who bought X also bought Y' pattern, why does the query include `WHERE NOT (target)-[:PURCHASED]->(rec)`?
options: To exclude products the target customer has already purchased, so recommendations are genuinely new
To ensure only the target customer's own purchases are returned
To delete the target customer's purchase history
This clause has no functional effect on the query
questions.explain: Without this filter, the query would recommend products the target already owns — the NOT clause filters those out.

questions.q: Does the classic 'bought X also bought Y' recommendation pattern require the Graph Data Science library?
options: No — it can be expressed as a plain two-hop Cypher traversal with no GDS algorithms involved
Yes — it is only possible using gds.nodeSimilarity
Yes — it requires the PageRank algorithm specifically
No — it requires abandoning Cypher entirely for a different query language
questions.explain: The lesson demonstrates this as a real, production-viable plain Cypher pattern, entirely separate from the GDS similarity procedures.

questions.q: What is the practical benefit of precomputing similarity scores offline and writing them back as a SIMILAR_TO relationship?
options: The expensive similarity computation runs once offline, so the request-time query is just a cheap traversal through the precomputed edges
It permanently deletes the original PURCHASED relationships
It eliminates the need for any Cypher queries at request time
It has no performance benefit over computing similarity live on every request
questions.explain: This is the standard production pattern the lesson describes: precompute expensive similarity offline, then serve it as a fast traversal at request time.
